ORBITAL LAYER / CONCEPTAVOCADOMINI RECEIVER PATH

THE MISSION

Orbit sends the signal.
avocadoMini brings it into the room.

Rocket Star is a planned orbital network that links a compact satellite constellation to compatible avocadoMini hardware.

One physical system. A new capability delivered through RockstarOS when the certified receiver path and orbital service are ready.

ORBIT

01 / LAUNCH

Build a compact
orbital layer.

Multiple Rocket Star vehicles form the planned first communication layer. The final spacecraft, launch provider, orbit, and deployment count remain design decisions.

MISSION ARCHITECTURE / CONCEPT

02 / RELAY

Many vehicles.
One signal path.

The constellation is designed to relay service across spacecraft and ground systems before reaching a compatible avocadoMini receiver.

COVERAGE, LATENCY, AND CAPACITY ARE NOT YET VALIDATED

03 / RECEIVE

From orbit
to the room.

A certified radio and antenna path is required inside supported hardware. A software update cannot replace radio hardware that is not already present.

RF HARDWARE + CERTIFICATION + NETWORK ACCESS REQUIRED

04 / ACTIVATE

New capability,
through RockstarOS.

After hardware validation, licensing, and service availability, a future RockstarOS update is intended to configure the receiver and expose Rocket Star connectivity.

AVOCADOMINI / RECEIVER PATH

The hardware stays.
The network arrives.

Rocket Star is being designed around an update-ready avocadoMini receiver path. Supported models would use integrated, certified radio hardware; RockstarOS would handle activation, network configuration, and service status.
